historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (1.0%, FY2020-25) lifted to ~3% average over the horizon for a repair-and-remodel recovery from a cyclical trough (existing-home turnover at multi-decade lows since 2023); equity CAGR is undefined because book equity is negative
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR cannot be computed: shareholders' equity went from +$421m (FY2020) to -$185m (FY2025) and -$365m (Q2-2026) because buybacks (~$4.0bn FY2021-25) exceeded retained earnings. This is a capital-structure artefact, not a business signal; revenue and owner-FCF CAGRs are used instead. Revenue 3yr CAGR (-4.5%) measures the FY2022 peak to the FY2025 trough and should not be extrapolated either way.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes (interest income not deducted: net-debt company). Series: FY2020 839-45-25=769; FY2022 616-49-17=550; FY2025 866-30-10=826. The 3-year owner-FCF CAGR (14.5%) is off the FY2022 working-capital trough and the 5-year figure (1.4%) is the honest one. Owner-FCF CAGR exceeds reported-FCF CAGR over 5 years because SBC fell from $45m to $30m; SBC is ~0.5% of revenue and immaterial to the valuation. FY2020 EPS ($4.60) includes gains on the Cabinetry and Windows divestitures, which depresses the 5-year EPS CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: Repair-and-remodel demand (~89-90% of sales) bottoms in 2026 after four years of volume decline (FY2026 sales up low-single-digits on pricing, North American volumes still negative) and recovers from 2027 as lower mortgage rates release pent-up housing turnover; Masco grows a point or two above the market on Delta/Behr share gains and pricing, with EBITDA margin returning to the FY2024 ~19.3% level and edging to ~19.8% on cost savings. Capital allocation stays dividends plus ~$600m/yr of buybacks, so the per-share compounding comes from the count, not from book equity. The one-off tariff refund is treated as cash in the bridge, not as margin.
scenario_narratives.bull: Housing turnover rebounds hard (existing-home sales back toward 5m from ~4m) and the deferred-project backlog converts into two to three years of 6% growth; tariff relief and cost programmes hold, so operating leverage takes EBITDA to ~21% (OI ~19%, the company's long-run aspiration). Hansgrohe's European recovery and premium mix add to it. Terminal growth 3% but the 15x cyclical cap still binds, so the bull case is mainly a flows story.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2027 R&R recovery does not arrive: rates stay high, big-ticket remodel spending falls another 4%, Behr loses DIY share at Home Depot (Masco's largest customer, ~35% of sales) and tariffs on China-sourced plumbing and hardware re-escalate without full price recovery, compressing EBITDA to 16.5% before a partial recovery to 17.5%. Buybacks slow to protect the BBB rating given the shareholders' deficit, and the leadership transition (new CEO and CFO, reorganised executive committee in January 2026, senior Plumbing and operations retirements through 2026) costs a year of execution. Terminal growth 2%; no scenario hits the zero-FCF floor -- the business remains solidly cash generative even here.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on consolidated flows with SBC (~0.5% of revenue, immaterial) fully expensed and the share count flat; a 10-year explicit build so the margin recovery is matured before capitalising; a 15x cyclical terminal cap; WACC 9% in all scenarios with cycle risk carried in the scenario paths and weights. The bridge is EV less June-2026 net debt less the Hansgrohe minority at 15x earnings, adjusted for the H1-2026 cash already spent on buybacks; book equity is negative and plays no role. House and street values nearly coincide because SBC is tiny.
key_risks_to_valuation: Repair-and-remodel cycle: the base case assumes turnover recovers from 2027; every year of delay is roughly $2-3/share.
Customer concentration: Home Depot ~35% of sales (Behr is exclusive to Home Depot); a paint reset or private-label push would hit the Decorative segment's 20%+ margins directly.
Tariffs and sourcing: plumbing and hardware are substantially sourced from China/Asia; the ~$85m IEEPA refund is treated as one-off, and re-escalation is the bear axis.
Leverage with negative book equity: ~$3.2bn debt, BBB rating, buybacks funded partly by a term loan; a downgrade would force buybacks to pause and raise the cost of debt.

Terminal-cap sensitivity: the 15x cap binds in base and bull; at a 16-18x exit (Masco's own 10-year EV/EBITDA has run 10-13x, i.e. ~18-22x owner FCF) the value is materially higher -- the gap is the price of not assuming re-rating.
Hansgrohe minority valued at 15x NCI earnings in the bridge; at book ($247m) the value is ~$2.4/share higher.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 58.16-83.64
data_sources.financials: MAS_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2006-Q1 2026, USD millions) for history; FY2025 10-K and Q2-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-29, accession 0000062996-26-000027) read directly for the 2026-06-30 balance sheet, share count, NCI, H1 cash flows and ASR; SEC companyfacts API for SBC, withholding taxes, cash taxes, D&A, leases and interest.
data_sources.qualitative: Q2-2026 earnings release (8-K ex-99.1, 2026-07-29) for FY2026 guidance and the IEEPA refund; MAS_Analysis.json was not yet available at build time.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 197.19m common shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover at 2026-06-30, less 0.8m shares delivered 2026-07-27 at no further cost to settle the $300m May-2026 ASR (the cash and the term loan funding it are already in the June balance sheet), plus ~1.0m dilutive options/RSUs (FY2025 dilutive effect per the EPS note). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it. Buybacks ($596m in H1-2026, $571m FY2025) fund the flat count and more; they are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: stock-based compensation add-back $30m (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation) plus employee withholding taxes paid on stock-based compensation $10m in financing (us-gaap:PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation). Masco publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. H1-2026 run-rate: $19m SBC + $14m withholding.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchase of common stock $571m (8.5m shares). H1-2026 $592m incl. the $300m ASR; new $2.0bn authorisation effective 2026-02-10, $1.9bn remaining at 2026-03-31. Actual cash, not authorisation.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 (cover), adjusted for the 2026-07-27 ASR final delivery
inputs.net_debt_note: Q2-2026 10-Q balance sheet: long-term debt $3,245m (incl. $300m two-year term loan drawn April-2026 to fund the ASR; FY2025 10-K $2,945m of senior notes) + notes payable $2m = $3,247m, less cash and cash investments $548m = $2,699m. Operating lease liabilities ($268m at FY2025) are EXCLUDED because the lease cost is already inside EBITDA (see lease_treatment); finance leases ($14m) sit inside other long-term debt. June is Masco's seasonal receivables peak ($1,342m vs $1,028m at December), so roughly $300m of this net debt is working capital that unwinds in H2 -- that unwind is inside the FY2026 explicit-year flow, which is why the H1-2026 realised FCF is deducted in the equity bridge rather than the net debt being restated.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate: 10-year UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.2 x ERP 4.75% = cost of equity ~9.9%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (FY2025 interest paid $100m on ~$2.95bn; term loan at 4.5%), 3.8% after tax; weights ~84% equity / 16% debt at market (market cap ~$13.5bn, net debt $2.7bn) -> WACC 8.9%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: housing-cycle risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the discount rate (adaptations section f).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: the $63m FY2025 operating lease cost is expensed inside operating profit, so it is already inside EBITDA and inside operating cash flow. Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: no separate lease_cost_pct_path, and operating lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. Finance leases are $14m and immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: Masco consolidates Hansgrohe SE with a ~32% minority. FY2025 net income attributable to NCI $48m (H1-2026 $30m) on consolidated flows; NCI dividends paid $45m. Charged ONCE, in the equity bridge: the NCI is deducted at 15x FY2025 NCI earnings = $720m (book value $247m at 2026-06-30 understates a claim on a premium European plumbing brand). The flows themselves stay consolidated, so no leakage is folded into the tax rate.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (scripts/dcf_engine.py via make build-dcf), with the cyclical adaptations read (owner-fcf-adaptations.md: risk charged once, leases, NCI). Masco is an operating company -- branded plumbing (Delta, Hansgrohe) and decorative architectural products (Behr paint, Liberty hardware) sold ~89-90% into repair-and-remodel -- so the owner-FCF stream is the right thing to discount. Negative book equity (-$365m shareholders' deficit at 2026-06-30, -$185m at FY2025) is the result of ~$4bn of buybacks over five years funded partly by debt; it is a capital-structure choice, not a solvency signal (interest cover ~12x, net debt/EBITDA ~1.9x, BBB credit, maturities laddered 2027-2032). The equity bridge therefore ignores book equity entirely: EV less net debt less NCI, both at the 2026-06-30 balance sheet. Equity CAGRs are undefined for the same reason and are reported null. FY0 is FY2025 actuals; Y1 is FY2026 built from guidance (GAAP EPS $4.21-4.41, adjusted $4.40-4.60 incl. ~$85m one-off IEEPA tariff refund benefit; underlying adjusted range $4.10-4.30 was reaffirmed). Because the balance sheet and share count are taken at 2026-06-30 while FY2026 is a full explicit year, the H1-2026 unlevered owner FCF already realised ($367m) is deducted in the bridge so it is not counted twice; the after-tax tariff refund is added there as a one-off rather than being left in the margin path. Owner FCF FY2025 = 866 reported FCF - 40 SBC incl. withholding - 0 interest income (net debt company, interest income immaterial and not deducted) = 826. Price is a regular close, not after-hours. Latest 10-Q is Q2-2026 (filed 2026-07-29); the SEC XBRL API and the Metrics CSV stop at Q1-2026, so the June anchors were read from the 10-Q document itself.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +1%: guidance is net sales up low-single-digits on a 'roughly flat' global R&R market plus pricing; H1 printed +2% (Q1 +6.5% on pricing/pre-tariff loading, Q2 -3%) so H2 is modelled roughly flat. FY2027-29 +4-4.5% as mortgage-rate relief and the unwinding of the rate lock-in lift existing-home turnover and R&R project spend from a four-year volume decline (management cites >$20bn of pent-up demand); tapering to 2.5% nominal.
base.margin_note: FY2025 EBITDA 18.5% (OI 16.5% + D&A 2.0%). FY2026 guidance is operating margin ~18%, of which ~1.1pp is the one-off IEEPA refund (~$85m on ~$7.6bn), so underlying OI ~16.9% -> EBITDA 18.9% here; the refund is added once in the equity bridge instead. Matures to 19.8% (OI ~17.8%) on volume leverage, Masco Operating System cost savings and mix; FY2024 already printed 19.3%, so this is a return to recent form, not a stretch.
base.tax_note: GAAP ETR 24.3-25.1% (Q2-2026/Q2-2025), normalised rate 24.5% in the company's adjusted EPS; FY2025 cash taxes $236m were 20.8% of pre-tax on timing. 24% flat on unlevered EBIT.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer/distributor: receivables + inventory exceed payables + accrued by ~7-17% of revenue depending on season, so growth consumes cash: capture -12% of the revenue change.
base.capex_note: Capex 2.1% of revenue FY2024-25 (3.0% in FY2023), D&A 2.0%; 2.2% keeps capex modestly above D&A through the growth years.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 shifted to 20/50/30. Bear up to 20%: Masco carries a shareholders' deficit and ~1.9x net debt/EBITDA with no balance-sheet cushion, a single customer near 35% of sales, direct exposure to China-sourced tariffs, and a demand base that has already fallen three years without the forecast recovery arriving. Bull down to 30%: the bull case needs housing turnover, tariff relief and share gains all to land together. Base 50%: FY2026 guidance was reaffirmed on an underlying basis and margins are being held through the volume trough.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
